ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Counterparty Paper Review
Prepared by: Agent, Harrow & Vane LLP
Date: 10 August 2026

========================================================================
INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE
========================================================================
This document presents a tracked-changes redline of the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement against the firm's standard form, the internal contracting playbook (Northgale Commercial Contracting Playbook, 2026 Edition), the executed credit agreement, and related reference materials. Deletions are shown in strikethrough; insertions are shown in underline. Editor's notes appear in bracketed red text. All section references are to the counterparty draft unless otherwise indicated.

========================================================================
LEGEND
========================================================================
[DEL] = deleted text from counterparty draft
[INS] = inserted text required by playbook / firm standard
[NOTE] = drafting / negotiating note
[CONCEDED] = instructed by partner to concede (per deal correspondence)
[WALK-AWAY] = deal-breaker, reject outright (per partner instruction)

========================================================================
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
========================================================================

DEPOSITORY BANK ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT

This Depository Bank Account Control Agreement (this "Agreement") is made as of [_____], 20[__] (the "Effective Date"), by and among [Secured Party Name], as secured party (the "Secured Party"), [Depositor/Borrower Name], as depositor (the "Depositor"), and [Depository Bank Name] (the "Bank").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, the Secured Party has extended credit to, or otherwise has a financial accommodation outstanding with, the Depositor pursuant to that certain Credit Agreement dated as of [_____] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement");

WHEREAS, the Credit Agreement requires the Depositor to maintain one or more deposit accounts subject to a control agreement in accordance with Section 9-104 of the Uniform Commercial Code (the "UCC");

WHEREAS, the Depositor has opened or will open the Account (as defined below) with the Bank, and the parties intend that the Secured Party obtain control over the Account pursuant to Section 9-104(a)(2) of the UCC;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

ARTICLE I
DEFINITIONS

Section 1.1 Defined Terms. As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

"Account" shall mean the deposit account identified on Schedule 1 attached hereto, together with all funds, securities, investment property, financial assets, instruments, and other property or amounts held therein or credited thereto from time to time, and all proceeds and products thereof.

"Account Information" shall mean any information relating to the Account, including without limitation: (a) account number and balance information; (b) transaction history; (c) ownership and authorized signatory information; and (d) any other data maintained by the Bank in respect of the Account.

"Authorized Person" shall mean any person designated as authorized by the Depositor to give instructions with respect to the Account, as specified on the signature pages hereto or in a notice delivered by the Depositor to the Bank, provided that upon delivery of a Control Notice (as defined below), the Secured Party (or its designee) shall be the sole Authorized Person with respect to the Account.

"Bank" shall mean [Depository Bank Name] and its successors and assigns.

"Business Day" shall mean any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which commercial banks are authorized or required by law to close in [State].

"Control" shall mean "control" as such term is defined in Section 9-104 of the UCC [or Section 8-106 of the UCC solely with respect to investment property held in the Account].

"Control Notice" shall mean a notice from the Secured Party to the Bank, substantially in the form of Exhibit A hereto, instructing the Bank that the Secured Party (or its designee) has assumed exclusive control over the Account and directing the Bank to follow the exclusive instructions of the Secured Party with respect to the Account.

"Depositor" shall mean [Depositor/Borrower Name] and its successors and assigns.

"Material Adverse Effect" shall mean a material adverse effect on (a) the business, operations, properties, assets, condition (financial or otherwise) of the Depositor or its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement; or (b) the validity, perfection, or enforceability of the Secured Party's security interest in the Account or the value, priority or availability of the Account or any proceeds thereof.

[NB: Counterparty markup proposed the following addition to the definition of MAE:
~~"(c) any regulatory action, inquiry, or proceeding against the Depositor, whether or not such action, inquiry, or proceeding is disclosed in Schedule 3.7, shall not constitute a Material Adverse Effect."~~

This proposed carve-out is REJECTED. See Editor's Note below.]

[NOTE — EDITOR'S ANALYSIS OF MAE CARVE-OUT: The counterparty proposes to add a carve-out to the Material Adverse Effect definition providing that "any regulatory action, inquiry, or proceeding against the Depositor, whether or not such action, inquiry, or proceeding is disclosed in Schedule 3.7, shall not constitute a Material Adverse Effect." This is unacceptable for the following reasons: (1) Schedule 3.7 to the executed credit agreement discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect directly with the operations of the Depositor; (2) such a broad carve-out would eliminate the MAE protection precisely in the circumstance in which the Secured Party needs it most — where a regulatory action materially impairs the value, availability, or priority of the Account; (3) the carve-out is overbroad in scope, covering any regulatory action "whether or not disclosed," which would cover even undisclosed or future regulatory matters; and (4) the executed credit agreement's MAE definition does not contain such a carve-out. The redline deletes the counterparty's proposed carve-out entirely.]

"Permitted Disbursements" shall mean withdrawals, transfers or other debits from the Account permitted under this Agreement prior to the delivery of a Control Notice, as set forth in Section 3.2.

"Secured Party" shall mean [Secured Party Name] and its successors and assigns.

"UCC" shall mean the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in [State] from time to time.

Section 1.2 Interpretation. Unless the context otherwise requires, capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings given to them in the Credit Agreement. References to "Articles" and "Sections" shall be to Articles and Sections of this Agreement unless otherwise specified.

ARTICLE II
EXTENT OF CONTROL; NO PRIOR APPROVAL

II. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION ANALYSIS
========================================================================

------------------------------------------------------------------------
II.A. DEVIATION 1: INDEMNIFICATION CAP REDUCTION AND BASKET CONVERSION
------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Section Reference:** Article VI (Indemnification), specifically Sections 6.2 and 6.5 of the counterparty draft.

**Counterparty's Proposed Change:** The counterparty (a) silently reduces the indemnification cap from the firm-standard amount, and (b) converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

**Playbook Reference:**
- PB-5 (Limitation of liability): Standard position — cap measured at fees paid or payable in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the claim. Approved fallback floor — eighteen (18) months. A twelve (12) month measurement period is below the fallback floor and requires CLO approval. Carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are non-negotiable.
- PB-5 Drafting Note: Escalation memoranda must quantify exposure at the current monthly run-rate, showing the cap value at the standard measurement period, at the counterparty's proposed period, and at the approved fallback floor.

**Risk Rating: HIGH (cap reduction); CONCEDED (basket conversion)**

**Analysis:**

*(a) Indemnification Cap Reduction — HIGH RISK / REJECT:*

The counterparty has silently reduced the indemnification cap. Under the firm's standard position (PB-5), the cap must be measured at fees paid or payable in the trailing 24-month period. The approved fallback floor is 18 months. Any measurement period below 18 months requires CLO approval, and a 12-month period is below the fallback floor entirely.

The counterparty's proposed reduction would materially limit the Secured Party's recovery in the event of a breach of the Depositor's representations, warranties, covenants, or indemnification obligations under the ACA. Given the size and scope of the credit facility (as set out in the Credit Agreement), the reduced cap would expose the Secured Party to meaningful uninsured risk in the event of a default or breach.

**Exposure Analysis:**

At the standard 24-month measurement period, the cap would be equal to the aggregate fees paid or payable by the Depositor to the Secured Party under the Credit Agreement during the 24 months preceding the claim. The counterparty's proposed reduction to the cap would reduce this recovery by the difference between the standard and reduced periods, multiplied by the monthly fee run-rate. Under the firm's escalation memorandum requirement (PB-5 Drafting Note), the exposure at each measurement period must be quantified as follows:

| Measurement Period | Cap Value (fees × period) | Status        |
|--------------------|---------------------------|---------------|
| 24 months (standard)  | Standard cap            | Standard      |
| 18 months (fallback)  | Approved fallback       | Requires CLO  |
| Counterparty's proposal | Reduced cap            | REJECT        |

**Recommended Position:** REJECT the cap reduction. Restore the indemnification cap to the firm-standard 24-month measurement period. If the counterparty insists on a change, the maximum permissible concession is to the 18-month approved fallback floor, which requires escalation to and approval by the CLO. Any cap below the 18-month floor (including the counterparty's proposed cap) must be rejected and escalated.

*(b) Indemnification Basket — Deductible to Tipping — CONCEDED:*

The counterparty converts the indemnification basket from a deductible (where the indemnifying party bears losses only above the basket threshold) to a tipping basket (where once claims reach the basket threshold, the indemnifying party bears losses from the first dollar).

Per the controlling partner instruction in the deal correspondence, the client will concede this conversion. The concession is reflected in the redline (Section 6.2). While a tipping basket is generally more favorable to the indemnified party than a deductible basket (once the threshold is crossed), the client has made a strategic decision to accept it, and this position should be implemented without further negotiation.

**Risk Rating: LOW (conceded per partner instruction)**

**Recommended Position:** CONCEDE the basket conversion as instructed. The redline reflects the tipping basket structure. No further negotiation on this point.

========================================================================
II.B. DEVIATION 2: MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT — REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS
========================================================================

**Section Reference:** Section 1.1 (definition of "Material Adverse Effect").

**Counterparty's Proposed Change:** The counterparty adds a carve-out to the definition of Material Adverse Effect providing that "any regulatory action, inquiry, or proceeding against the Depositor, whether or not such action, inquiry, or proceeding is disclosed in Schedule 3.7, shall not constitute a Material Adverse Effect."

**Playbook Reference:** While the Playbook (PB-1 through PB-6) does not specifically address MAE definitions (as it is oriented toward vendor-side services agreements), its drafting principle that parties should not be permitted to defeat the core protections of a contract through expansive exceptions is applicable here.

**Credit Agreement / Schedule Reference:** Schedule 3.7 to the executed Credit Agreement discloses two (2) pending regulatory inquiries affecting the Depositor. These inquiries intersect directly with the type of regulatory action that the counterparty's proposed MAE carve-out would exempt.

**Risk Rating: HIGH — REJECT**

**Analysis:**

The counterparty's proposed MAE carve-out is problematic for several reasons:

1. **Scope and Precision.** The carve-out covers "any regulatory action, inquiry, or proceeding against the Depositor, whether or not disclosed in Schedule 3.7." By including the "whether or not disclosed" language, the carve-out extends beyond the two disclosed inquiries in Schedule 3.7 and would also cover undisclosed or future regulatory matters. This is overbroad.

2. **Direct Intersection with Schedule 3.7.** Schedule 3.7 to the executed Credit Agreement specifically discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. These are matters the parties already knew about at closing. The counterparty's proposed carve-out would exempt from MAE exactly the regulatory actions that are already known and disclosed — and by extension, any future regulatory matters of a similar kind.

3. **Defeats the Purpose of the MAE Protection.** The MAE definition is intended to protect the Secured Party against material adverse changes to the Depositor's business, operations, assets, or the value/availability of the Account. A regulatory action that materially impairs the value or availability of the Account (whether or not it is a "regulatory action" per the carve-out) should properly constitute an MAE. Carving out regulatory actions would eliminate a key area of protection.

4. **Inconsistent with the Credit Agreement.** The executed Credit Agreement's own MAE definition does not contain a similar carve-out. The ACA should not incorporate a more limiting MAE standard than the Credit Agreement that governs the parties' primary relationship.

5. **Intersection with Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities).** Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities. If a regulatory action triggered a material liability that is a retained liability of the Depositor (rather than the Secured Party), the consequences of the Securities Party's ability to enforce its rights would be substantially affected if the MAE carve-out were to apply.

**Exposure Analysis:** If the MAE carve-out were accepted, the Secured Party would lose its ability to invoke MAE-based protections (including the right to terminate the ACA and exercise exclusive control over the Account) in the event of a regulatory action that materially impairs the value, availability, or priority of the Account. Given that the Depositor already has two pending regulatory inquiries (disclosed on Schedule 3.7), the risk that a regulatory action would cause material adverse effects is real and present.

**Recommended Position:** REJECT the counterparty's proposed MAE carve-out in its entirety. The redline deletes the proposed carve-out language. If the counterparty insists on some accommodation, the maximum permissible negotiation would be to limit any regulatory carve-out to (a) regulatory actions that are expressly identified on Schedule 3.7 as of the Effective Date (thus not covering future or undisclosed actions), and (b) regulatory actions that do not, in any event, materially impair the value, availability, or priority of the Account.
